decision: Use the recovered official Silliman Journal record and selected indexed article text to improve discovery and preserve the author-reported fish names as historical candidates. Do not allocate aggregate lists to an individual waterbody, silently correct source taxonomy, or add app assertions. The full site-by-site tables and item-specific reuse approval remain unavailable.

source.title: Endemic, Indigenous, and Introduced Species in the Freshwater Ecosystems of Nueva Ecija and Pampanga: Status, Diversity, and Impacts
source.dateInterpretation: The OJS article page displays a 2022 published field while the issue cover and citation identify Volume 50(2), July-December 2009. Preserve both; use the issue date for the article's publication context and do not infer a 2022 field survey.

accessReview.officialArticlePage: Opened; abstract and author/issue metadata reviewed.
accessReview.officialIssuePdf: The official 218-page issue PDF was opened through the journal's issue download route. Its front matter confirms 2009 copyright and all-rights-reserved terms.
accessReview.articlePdfRoute: The article-specific route returned HTTP 502 during this review. Publisher-indexed text from the official article PDF exposed the abstract and selected results/table excerpts; a complete local PDF or text extraction was not obtained or retained.
accessReview.tableReviewScope: Selected text only: Table 1 names and limited site columns, and Table 5 source labels were visible in the publisher-indexed excerpt. Neither table was fully transcribed.
accessReview.reuse: The issue says copyright is held by individual authors and Silliman Journal and all rights are reserved. The publisher's editorial policy requires written permission from both journal and author to reproduce an article in full, quote more than 500 words, or copy two or more tables/figures; it notes conditions and fees may apply. No item-specific open license or reuse permission was verified.
accessReview.researchDisposition: Only factual author-reported fish-name strings and bounded aggregate counts are retained for internal source triage. No SIV values, table structure, article prose, image or public/app content is reproduced. Public-app permission remains unapproved pending item-specific rights and qualified review.

stationMethod.newEcija: Three designated stations per study area and ten randomly selected 10 m by 12 m quadrats at each station.
stationMethod.pampanga: Ten stations per study area according to the abstract.

sourceReportedStudyDesign.taxonomicIdentification: The study reports survey, collection, identification, description and classification of aquatic organisms. Methods and voucher records were not independently cross-checked in this limited access follow-up.

sourceReportedAggregateCounts.warning: These counts include aquatic organisms beyond fish and are the paper's historical totals. They are not site-specific fish counts, present-day diversity or comparable directly with other studies.

interpretationLimits: These are source-era taxon strings, not independently accepted modern names or voucher-confirmed identities.
New Ecija lists are aggregate across five ecosystems; do not assign names to Paitan, Pantabangan, Tabuating, Talavera or Palayan individually from this excerpt.
The Pampanga/Candaba introduced-species table combines Candaba Swamp and Pampanga River; do not infer which individual river reach or wetland contains each listed taxon.
The source's Hypopthalmichthys spelling is preserved verbatim and must not be silently corrected.
Introduced/native/endemic classifications are the article's source-era labels and are not current country-wide status determinations.

crossStudyContext.comparisonDecision: The 2006 NAST and 2009 Silliman studies overlap in authors and Nueva Ecija sites but report differently scoped aggregate richness. Treat them as related historical sources, not independent estimates; do not sum their counts or resolve species conflicts without the full tables and taxonomy review.
crossStudyContext.candabaDecision: The newly surfaced 2009 names complement the 2020/2010/1988 source leads but do not override their conflicts or establish current Candaba presence. Keep the wetland's historical inventories separate.

nextStep: Continue site-specific fish-source discovery for Central Luzon while keeping the one GBIF/Catalog family conflict and all Silliman specimen/locality questions held. Do not assign aggregate fish names to sites or release them to the app until source rows, identity, locality and rights are verified.
